The guest-side fixings Cua Driver needs on a Wayland desktop: the udev rule
that makes /dev/uinput group-accessible (the isolated-background-input route),
and — only where netplan exists — a DHCP netplan so a cloud/containerDisk guest
leases on whatever NIC the hypervisor presents (enp1s0 under KubeVirt, ens3
under QEMU). On NetworkManager distros the netplan is skipped. Verifiable on
the built image: the udev rule is present and the input group exists.

## Acceptance plan

This candy's `plan:` — the runnable spec `charly check` executes against a live deployment. `check:` steps are idempotent probes; `run:` steps change state.

| Intent | Step |
|---|---|
| `run` | install the uinput udev rule (the isolated-background-input route needs a group-accessible /dev/uinput) |
| `run` | write the DHCP netplan so a cloud/containerDisk guest leases on the hypervisor NIC (netplan distros only) |
| `check` | the uinput udev rule is installed (the isolated-input route needs it) |
| `check` | the netplan was written only where netplan exists (correct on both NetworkManager and netplan distros) |
